paras: The attack on Moses Banks was the beating and pursuit of a Black man by a crowd of white men and boys at a baseball game in Woodstock, Virginia, on 20 May 1903. Banks escaped to a house, where the police chief and the mayor took him to jail. The local Shenandoah Herald, its only known reporter, called it "a small taste of race riot" and urged young Black residents to leave town.

On Wednesday afternoon a colored team from Front Royal was playing a Woodstock team on the commons before white spectators. According to the Herald, Black girls crowded in front of the white spectators, said "it was their day," and refused to move back.

The paper accused Banks of parading before the girls with a bat, applying "a vile name" to small white boys, and daring any white man to take it up. A crowd rushed him and beat him with clubs, baseball bats and stones, blows the Herald said "would have killed any white man." Banks fled across the commons, chased by about 75 white men and boys.

He hid upstairs in the house of Joe Hardin, whom the paper called "uncle Joe." Because Hardin's wife was seriously ill, he asked the crowd not to enter, and it hesitated. Chief of Police Koontz and Mayor Chapman then arrived and put Banks in jail.

The fight broke up the game in the seventh inning, with Front Royal leading 29 to 5. Banks was the only person reported hurt; his injuries were not described. No report of a charge against Banks or an arrest of his attackers was found.

The Herald ran the story on 22 May under the headline "DARK TOWN WAS OUT" and the subhead "ONLY ONE NEGRO HURT." Told from the crowd's side, it called Banks a "young buck" and "Mr. Coon" and said of his challenge, "He was accommodated." It said young Black men and girls who "think that their day has come" should "shake the dust of Woodstock from their feet."
No other white or Black report of the attack was found.

reader.title: Attack on Moses Banks
bases: A crowd beat Moses Banks with clubs, bats and stones and chased him to a house, where officials arrested him; no killing, threat to kill or talk of lynching is reported (A1).
Banks escaped the crowd of about 75 and was jailed alive, with 'only one negro hurt'; the crowd acted without authority over an alleged insult, but no one was killed (A1).
The only report is the local Shenandoah Herald, a white weekly whose account is written from the crowd's side (A1).

accounts.label: Local white paper (crowd's side)
accounts.gist: Black girls refused to yield space to white spectators and Banks insulted white boys and dared white men to respond; the crowd beat and chased him until officials jailed him.

framing.detail: Under 'DARK TOWN WAS OUT,' the Herald called Banks a 'young buck' and 'Mr. Coon', said he was 'accommodated', and told young Black people to 'shake the dust of Woodstock from their feet'.

record_check.dossier: mob_assault: a beating and chase with no killing, threat to kill or mention of lynching
The paper never speaks of lynching or killing intent; at most the crowd's pursuit to the house could be read as threatening
About 75 white men and boys at the ball game, unnamed
Beating and pursuit; the crowd gathered at the house but hesitated and did not enter, so 'siege' overstates it
In pursuit during the attack; then taken to jail by the police chief and mayor (the victim, not attackers, was arrested)
The paper justified the attack: Banks's alleged insult and challenge, and Black girls claiming 'it was their day'

info: Wednesday afternoon, 20 May 1903 (the Wednesday before the Friday 22 May issue)
The commons at Woodstock, during a baseball game between a colored team from Front Royal and a Woodstock team; ended at Joe Hardin's house
Moses Banks, a Black man called a 'young buck' by the paper

Accused by the paper of parading before Black girls with a bat, applying 'a vile name' to small white boys and saying any white man who wanted to take it up should come out, after Black girls refused to move back from in front of white spectators
A crowd of white men and boys at the game; none named
Banks jailed; game broken up in the 7th inning with Front Royal leading 29 to 5

sources.note: Local weekly's only account: crowd of about 75 white men and boys beat and chased Moses Banks at a colored ball game on the Woodstock commons; police chief and mayor jailed him.
quotes: WOODSTOCK HAS A SMALL TASTE OF RACE RIOT—ONLY ONE NEGRO HURT.
a wild rush was made for him and he was beat with clubs, base ball bats and stones, which would have killed any white man.
the crowd hesitated in going into the house to bring Mr. Coon out.
We must agree with them that their day has come to shake the dust of Woodstock from their feet and beat a hasty retreat.
